_: Cards authored from the two Nihongo 102 PDFs, Phase 2 of the absorption. Keyed by destination unit. Every card is aiSuggested with a reviewNote naming its PDF and the job it does.

chapter-2-extras.note: かいしゃ (kaisha) 'company' plus いん (in), the suffix for a member of staff. Names the job the way you would answer 'what do you do?'.
chapter-2-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: an occupation word the book never teaches, built on かいしゃ (kaisha) from this lesson.

chapter-2-extras.note: だれ (dare) on its own is just the word 'who'; だれですか (dare desu ka) is the whole question.
chapter-2-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the class taught the question-word set as complete ですか (desu ka) questions; the book cards only the bare word だれ (dare).

chapter-3-extras.note: いつ (itsu) plus ですか (desu ka). Unlike なんじですか (nan-ji desu ka) it does not demand a clock time, so a day on its own answers it.
chapter-3-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the whole question, where the book cards only the bare word いつ (itsu).

chapter-5-extras.hint: the short question on its own, ending in ですか (desu ka)
chapter-5-extras.note: どこ (doko) plus ですか (desu ka). Asks which place something is.
chapter-5-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the whole question, where the book cards only the bare word どこ (doko). Carries a hint because 'Where is it?' also reaches どこにありますか (doko ni arimasu ka) in Lesson 13.

chapter-6-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: puts ジム (jimu), taught bare in Lesson 3, into a sentence using this lesson's に (ni) plus いきます (ikimasu).

chapter-6-extras.note: The first of four cards on one frame that change only the ending: いきます (ikimasu), いきました (ikimashita), いきません (ikimasen), いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita).
chapter-6-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF. Job: cell 1 of the いきます paradigm the PDF prints as a table, delivered as a fixed frame so only the inflection varies.

chapter-6-extras.target: かいしゃにいきました
chapter-6-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF. Job: cell 2 of the いきます paradigm. Added so the four-cell contrast is complete on one frame; the PDF lists the form and the book teaches it only on other sentences.

chapter-6-extras.english: I don't go to the office.
chapter-6-extras.target: かいしゃにいきません
chapter-6-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF. Job: cell 3 of the いきます paradigm, delivered as a sentence rather than the PDF's bare table row.

chapter-6-extras.english: I didn't go to the office.
chapter-6-extras.target: かいしゃにいきませんでした
chapter-6-extras.note: Past negative is built on いきません (ikimasen) plus でした (deshita), not on いきました (ikimashita).
chapter-6-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF. Job: cell 4 of the いきます paradigm, delivered as a sentence rather than the PDF's bare table row.

chapter-7-extras.hint: the 〜で (de) variant, not the usual form
chapter-7-extras.note: A variant of あるいて (aruite). Both mean going on foot, and あるいて (aruite) is the one you will hear.
chapter-7-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF, listed there as an alternative to あるいて (aruite). Worth a look at gate 1: if it is not a form you want to produce, exclude it and keep あるいて (aruite) alone.

chapter-7-extras.english: How do you get to the gym?
chapter-7-extras.target: どうやってジムにいきますか
chapter-7-extras.pronunciation: dō yatte jimu ni ikimasu ka
chapter-7-extras.note: どうやって (dō yatte) asks by what means, like なんで (nande) in this lesson. どうやって (dō yatte) is the more everyday of the two.
chapter-7-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF, which prints it schematically as どうやって〜にいきますか. Rewritten around ジム (jimu) because a shipped 〜 is not something a person can say.

chapter-7-extras.target: ジムにあるいていきます
chapter-7-extras.scene: answering how you get to the gym
chapter-7-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF. Job: the answer to the どうやって (dō yatte) question, showing あるいて (aruite) used as a means of going.

chapter-7-extras.english: How do you go to work?
chapter-7-extras.target: どうやってしごとにいきますか
chapter-7-extras.pronunciation: dō yatte shigoto ni ikimasu ka
chapter-7-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 3. Job: the same どうやって (dō yatte) frame with a second destination, so the learner sees a slot rather than a fixed phrase.

chapter-7-extras.english: I go to work by bus.
chapter-7-extras.target: バスでしごとにいきます
chapter-7-extras.scene: answering how you get to work
chapter-7-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 3 answer. Job: contrasts the で (de) of means against the あるいて (aruite) answer above.

chapter-8-extras.target: ばんごはんをたべます
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the bare を (o) plus たべます (tabemasu) frame on ばんごはん (bangohan), which this lesson teaches as a word.

chapter-8-extras.target: きのう、なにをたべましたか
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 2. Job: past-tense なにを (nani o) question, the form this lesson teaches.

chapter-8-extras.target: ハンバーガーをたべました
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 2 answer.

chapter-8-extras.english: What did you do last weekend?
chapter-8-extras.target: せんしゅうまつ、なにをしましたか
chapter-8-extras.note: せんしゅう (senshū) 'last week' plus まつ (matsu) 'end'. The lesson's own しゅうまつ (shūmatsu) is the weekend without saying which one.
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 4. Job: names a specific past weekend, where the lesson's しゅうまつになにをしましたか (shūmatsu ni nani o shimashita ka) leaves it open.

chapter-8-extras.target: えいがかんにいきました
chapter-8-extras.scene: answering what you did last weekend
chapter-8-extras.note: えいが (eiga) 'film' plus かん (kan), the suffix for a building.
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 4 answer. Job: the only sentence えいがかん (eigakan) appears in.

chapter-8-extras.english: What do you do on Sundays?
chapter-8-extras.target: にちようび、なにをしますか
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 5. Job: the present-tense なにを (nani o) question against the past-tense one above.

chapter-8-extras.target: にちようび、かじをします
chapter-8-extras.scene: answering what you do on Sundays
chapter-8-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 5 answer. Job: the only sentence かじ (kaji) appears in.

chapter-9-extras.note: おすすめ (osusume) from this lesson, joined to みせ (mise) with の (no).
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: puts this lesson's おすすめ (osusume) into a phrase rather than leaving it a bare noun.

chapter-9-extras.target: にほんごをべんきょうします
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the only sentence にほんご (nihongo), taught bare in this lesson, appears in.

chapter-9-extras.note: The ご (go) suffix turns a country into its language, the same way にほん (nihon) becomes にほんご (nihongo).
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: shows ご (go) is a productive suffix, not part of the fixed word にほんご (nihongo).

chapter-9-extras.note: Irregular against the pattern: it is えいご (eigo), not イギリスご (igirisugo), even though the country is イギリス (igirisu).
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the exception to the ご (go) suffix pattern, which is where a learner silently goes wrong.

chapter-9-extras.target: まいしゅうげつようび
chapter-9-extras.note: まいしゅう (maishū) 'every week' in front of a day names that day every week.
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: combines this lesson's まいしゅう (maishū) with a weekday from Lesson 7.

chapter-9-extras.english: What time do you get up every day?
chapter-9-extras.target: まいにち、なんじにおきますか
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 1. Job: this lesson's まいにち (mainichi) with a habitual verb, plus the に (ni) that marks a clock time.

chapter-9-extras.english: I get up at eight o'clock.
chapter-9-extras.target: わたしは、はちじにおきます
chapter-9-extras.scene: answering what time you get up
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 1 answer. Job: the second of the two sentences おきます (okimasu) appears in.

chapter-9-extras.english: How did you come here today?
chapter-9-extras.target: きょう、どうやってここにきましたか
chapter-9-extras.pronunciation: kyō dō yatte koko ni kimashita ka
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 6. Job: どうやって (dō yatte) in the past, on this lesson's ここ (koko).

chapter-9-extras.target: でんしゃでここにきました
chapter-9-extras.scene: answering how you got here today
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 6 answer. Job: the で (de) of means answering a どうやって (dō yatte) question in the past.

chapter-9-extras.english: What time did you go to bed last night?
chapter-9-extras.target: さくばん、なんじにねましたか
chapter-9-extras.note: さくばん (sakuban) is last night. きのうのよる (kinō no yoru) says the same thing more plainly.
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 7. Job: the past of the なんじに (nan-ji ni) time question, against the present-tense one above.

chapter-9-extras.english: I went to bed at twelve.
chapter-9-extras.target: じゅうにじにねました
chapter-9-extras.scene: answering what time you went to bed
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 7 answer. Job: the second of the two sentences ねました (nemashita) appears in.

chapter-10-extras.note: Sits in front of a noun without な (na), unlike the な-adjectives in this lesson: おなじみせ (onaji mise), not おなじなみせ (onaji na mise).
chapter-10-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a describing word that looks like a な-adjective and does not behave like one, which is where a learner goes wrong.

chapter-11-extras.note: The opposite of さいこう (saikō). Both are verdicts on how something turned out, so they answer どうでしたか (dō deshita ka).
chapter-11-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: an evaluative word answering this lesson's どうでしたか (dō deshita ka).

chapter-11-extras.note: The opposite of さいあく (saiaku). Stronger than いい (ii): it is the top of the scale, not merely good.
chapter-11-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: an evaluative word answering this lesson's どうでしたか (dō deshita ka).

chapter-14-extras.note: Answered with から (kara), the 'because' particle this lesson teaches.
chapter-14-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the question どうして (dōshite) asks, placed here because this is the lesson that teaches how to answer it.

chapter-15-extras.note: Built the same way as this lesson's イタリアりょうり (itaria ryōri): a country in front of りょうり (ryōri).
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a second example of the country plus りょうり (ryōri) pattern, so it reads as a slot rather than a fixed phrase.

chapter-15-extras.note: A noun plus する (suru), the dictionary form of します (shimasu). The polite form is かんこうします (kankō shimasu).
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a noun-plus-する (suru) verb in the dictionary form this lesson introduces.

chapter-15-extras.note: のる (noru) takes に (ni), not を (o): じてんしゃにのる (jitensha ni noru), never じてんしゃをのる (jitensha o noru).
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a dictionary-form verb on Lesson 7's じてんしゃ (jitensha), and the に (ni) it takes is the part a learner gets wrong.

chapter-15-extras.note: The pastime, so it works after すき (suki): サイクリングがすきです (saikuringu ga suki desu). じてんしゃにのる (jitensha ni noru) is the act of riding.
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: a hobby noun for this lesson's すき (suki) frame.

chapter-15-extras.english: I ate pizza with a friend.
chapter-15-extras.target: ともだちとピザをたべました
chapter-15-extras.scene: answering what you did last weekend
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Extra questions PDF, question 4 answer. Sits in this lesson rather than with its question because ピザ (piza) is taught here; the scene carries the question so the card is answerable alone.
